body:
MYK'S CALL, and the second one tonight of the same shape. T263's PR 10 cannot land without retiring a rail that is frozen.

WHAT PR 10 DOES. One condition in `registerStanding` (src/server/http.ts): a bound connection's register fence was the UNION of its container path and any prefix a `register` grant named for its key; PR 10 makes the binding decide alone. §58 has said the container is the whole grant from the start, and the union's own comment says it exists only until derived standing lands. It landed in PR 3.

WHY IT CANNOT LAND. `test/server/derived-standing.test.ts` carries a case titled "law under a GRANTED prefix still lands in the primary and serves everyone — nothing stops working before its replacement". It asserts that a bound connection holding a `zed:` grant is served `registerPrefixes: ["zed:", "ada:journal:"]` and registers `zed:thing` with a 200. PR 10 makes both false, by design. That file is a declared rail of T263 and stands on main, so rails-guard refuses an edit to it — correctly: a rail the change can rewrite is not a rail.

The case's own comment names this slice as the one that retires it. It was written to be retired, and nothing in the process lets a slice retire a frozen rail on its own word.

THREE MORE SURFACES GO STALE THE MOMENT THE UNION DOES, and PR 10 carried none of them. Each is a report that would become false:
- `cmdGrantMint` (src/cli/cli.ts) prints "granted <id> register standing under <prefix> — it may register schemas whose name starts with <prefix> and nothing else". For a bound connector that is now false: the delta lands and the door ignores it. H7 at the CLI, on the verb's most common target.
- The `loam_register` MCP tool description (src/server/http.ts) names the grant as the way a connection holds register standing, and never the container path — which after this change is the only way.
- `docs/register-grammar.md` and its compiled twin say "Who this is for. A connection holding a register grant". Both are served to bound connections over MCP.
- `spec/58-a-connection-is-a-peer.md` §58.3 states the union as what IS: "its standing is an operator's explicit register grant and never the binding's ... Until then a bound connection that holds a register grant shapes the store." The "until then" is now.

THE ROADS, so the choice is a real one:
- AUTHORIZE THE RAIL'S RETIREMENT. The case is retired and its surviving half — that granted law lands in the primary and serves everyone, for a key that is not a bound connection — moves to the new file. This is what the case's own comment anticipated, and it wants your word because nothing else can give it.
- LEAVE THE UNION. §58's promise is then narrower than the section says, and §58.3's paragraph stays true. Cheapest, and it leaves a store-wide prefix reachable by a bound connection forever.
- RETIRE THE VERB WHOLE. Bigger: the CLI mint goes too, which breaks the ledger rails of T205 and T230, which are also frozen. Not recommended tonight.

Acceptance criteria:
(a) A bound connection's register fence is its container alone, and an unbound key's grant is untouched. Verify: test/server/grant-retired.test.ts, already written, 1 red on main with two declared controls.
(b) The retired rail's surviving half is carried, not dropped: granted law still lands in the primary and serves everyone for a key that is not a bound connection. Verify: the new file, two-sided.
(c) No surface still reports the union. Verify: the CLI's own output, the tool description, docs/register-grammar.md, and §58.3, each with a rail or a diff.

Merge tier: MYK'S. It retires a frozen rail and narrows what an operator can hand out.

2026-09-06 RESUMPTION: Myk has explicitly authorized autonomous decisions otherwise gated by ceremony ("you have permission to make decisions that seem obvious but are only gated by ceremony here"). Apply the anticipated retirement: bound registration fence is only its container; an explicit unbound actor grant remains valid. Preserve and strengthen the surviving unbound primary/global-serving control. This narrows registration authorization, not imported-schema adoption; receiving bindings are a separate delta-derived mechanism (T281-T285). Complete all four reports, including bound CLI grant output that honestly records the key grant without promising to widen the binding. Keep unbound CLI output compatible.

Use an isolated resume/pr557 checkout at current main. Author and measure new server and bound-CLI tests before implementation. The existing derived-standing test must be revised only at its anticipated granted-prefix case: refuse out-of-container publication, prove no primary/pool/served law, retain container-success and mixed-name-refusal checks. Every other case remains byte-identical. Prepare its exact SHA256 authorization in scripts/rail-renames.json through the established two-PR base-only revisions mechanism; do not make a candidate branch self-authorize. The base authorization must land before candidate CI can accept the changed frozen rail. Standalone authorization and implementation are concrete reviewable artifacts, not a silent rail waiver. Acceptance still excludes merging without the required base authorization. New tests are frozen after authoring, existing case revision is openly declared, all unchanged behavior controls remain active.

New rails measured against unchanged main:2failed,1passed (actual out-of-fence200vs403 and stale bound CLI output; unbound primary/global-serving control passes). New tests lint-clean before implementation. Existing derived-standing file revision is confined to the anticipated union case; all other cases retained. Exact proposed rail hashes: {"test/server/grant-retired.test.ts": "14822f0923481e0961e5f48f97d531348d1e90aad3029337861591424b5e9aad", "test/cli/bound-grant-report.test.ts": "38ffee955827e61f2b9baff6883d7ddacca7875e78f5c959a4962252a0803bf3", "test/server/derived-standing.test.ts": "b17c10e26fc676daf719854b92b243cd232936fd671be0781d17b4a4cb0bb83f"}. Base-only authorization for the existing-file hash remains a separate required landing; this declaration does not waive it.

Independent P1 review required preserving connector-wide revocation semantics: bound mint text must not imply loam grant revoke leaves connector access standing. It will report the recorded key grant and unchanged binding fence, without the old next-request-refuses promise. Reviewed registerPrefixesOf already independently enforces store grant context, subject, register verb, prefix and operator authorship for the CLI persistence assertion. Strengthened unbound routing control before implementation: connect the bound bystander before publication, then assert primary law, no inbox copy, and both readers serve the field. Final authored hashes {"test/server/grant-retired.test.ts": "cd66c1cb2f1da89914fdb44c6cc90ab767554345da5b614d114d20734ecb12a1", "test/cli/bound-grant-report.test.ts": "38ffee955827e61f2b9baff6883d7ddacca7875e78f5c959a4962252a0803bf3", "test/server/derived-standing.test.ts": "b17c10e26fc676daf719854b92b243cd232936fd671be0781d17b4a4cb0bb83f"}.

Gemini P5 review and independent reproduction found another stale registration report in docs/first-steps.md and its compiled topic. Extend the documentation correction to onboarding: derive the namespace from loam_whoami registerPrefixes, use an explicit example container prefix throughout the exercises, and remove the bound connector grant/restart recipe. Unbound grant behavior stays supported. No runtime or frozen test changes are needed. This scope extension is authorized by the request to fix and loop on verified review findings.
title: PR 10 needs a frozen rail retired, and four surfaces still report the union
